This document presents terms and definitions for concepts relevant to the Metaverse.
Specifically, the terminology presented in this document:
serve as a sound basis in the understanding of Metaverse;
guide new developments in the field by underpinning mutual understanding; and
serve as a quick and handy reference for those newly introduced to this field.

fo:block.fox:title: Section 1 ​ Scope
fo:block.fo:block: This document provides a concept system and a standard set of terminology related to the Metaverse, from basic concepts to those of the Metaverse ecosystem.
The scope of the vocabulary provided in this document corresponds to that of ISO/IEC JSEG 15.

fo:block.fox:title: Section 2 ​ Normative references
fo:block.fo:block: There are no normative references in this document.

The definition of a “metaverse” has long been subject of controversy.
In order to define any concept, it is necessary to determine the essential characteristics of the concept, where additions or subtractions to these characteristics will no longer define the concept.
The word “metaverse” originated from the science fiction Snow Crash written by Neal Stephenson in 1992 Reference [34].

In popular culture, the term “metaverse” is commonly used as a generalized entity beyond the Internet, as a massively multi-player virtual world experienced through immersive technologies with comprehensive sensory integration through human computer interfaces.
The group has considered a few popular definitions of the “metaverse”, including:
From Reference [31]: “universal, immersive virtual world that is facilitated by virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR)”
From Reference [32]: persistent and immersive simulated world that is experienced in the first person by large groups of simultaneous users who share a strong sense of mutual presence
From Reference [33]: an infinite and persistent set of computer-generated virtual worlds that may be accessed via some human computer interface
WS 1 has considered various definitions, common perspectives and expectations on the term “metaverse” and has come to the following conclusions based on consensus.
as in the items in the experience is virtual
where it is experienced through human-​computer interaction
where the experience is spatially organized according to some notion of location
where users can directly interact with it and receive feedback
Common characteristics expected by popular culture include:
where there can be many simultaneous users
between users across virtual world systems
where actions and events in the virtual world persists after a user leaves
where user actions are performed in real-​time
The resulting consensus arrived at this definition for “metaverse”:
metaverse: interactive virtual world that incorporates spatial referencing experienced through immersive technologies
collective reference to both AR and VR
